profile.headline: Software Engineer at Cisco
profile.summary: While I have a PhD in Physical Chemistry, my research, internships, and fellowships involved writing a considerable amount of software. Since graduation, I've developed a variety of software and DevOps solutions across four freelance contracts. I was recently recruited by Cisco, where I am writing software and developing IT infrastructures to support their team of over 10,000 software engineers. My wife’s company requires us to move frequently until September 2017, so I am focusing on remote positions.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:

Infrastructure design and implementation for systems monitoring framework with predictive analytics.

positions.description:

positions.title: Online education problem framework developer
positions.description:
 Developed new custom problems based in JavaScript and jQuery UI that integrate with MITx|edX
 Authored chemistry problems and templates leveraging advanced functionality of the edX platform
 Provided technical support to professors and each semester’s group of teacher assista

positions.title: Research Assistant/PhD Candidate
positions.description:
 Contributed to various successful collaborative projects, serving as the primary theoretical scientist
 Wrote parallelized, object-oriented codes to run scientific calculations and visualize data, many of which are used by other members of the group
 Employed various quantum- and statistical-mechanical theories to devise physical models that explain and clarify experimental results

positions.title: Software Scientist/Engineer
positions.description:
(Summer internship)

 Developed new modules and data types for AiiDa, a python framework for automating and databasing computations
 Created modular workflows for automating Bosch's high-throughput materials computations
 Worked with a team of remote developers through Git.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
 Wrote modules that extended existing framework to calculate additional observables
 Developed new implementation of the lab’s main computational framework, which resulted in debugging and expedited project progress
 Taught senior lab member new coding practices

honors.title: MIT Energy Initiative Graduate Research Fellowship for Energy Recipient
honors.description: The Society of Energy Fellows at MIT mobilizes outstanding graduate students to help address the world's energy challenges. The Society was established in 2008 with the generous support of MITEI Founding, Sustaining, and Associate Members to help MIT address the world's energy challenges. The program is designed to attract and support graduate students with a special interest in energy, to build MIT's research capacity, and to foster a robust community of faculty, students, and staff engaged in energy research, education, and campus activity. Named MIT Energy Fellows at the master's and doctoral levels are selected on the basis of keen interest in energy, excellent academic record, and promising future. --From http://mitei.mit.edu/education/fellowships
honors.issuer: Issued by MIT Energy Initiative · Sep 2010

publications.title: The Role of Electron–Hole Separation in Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence in Donor–Acceptor Blends
Nanoscale transport of charge-transfer states in organic donor-acceptor blends

patents.title: PROCESSES IN THERMALLY ACTIVATED DELAYED FLUORESCENCE
patents.description: Alternative mechanism for applying a new technology that has the potential of improving organic LEDs (OLEDs) and ushering in a new era of solid state lighting.
